description_en: Located in the north-western corner of the Kathmandu Valley, the Newar settlement of Phusiṃkhyaḥ—also known as Manamaiju—reveres Indrāyaṇī as itsgrāmadevatā(kṣetrapāla). While the community worships her as its tutelary goddess, the Pradhāna  lineage of Thamel has long venerated the same deity as their privateiṣṭadevī.The site comprises both an innerdyaḥchẽwithin the settlement and the mainpīṭhalocated outside the village. Thepīṭhastands in an open field of roughly tenropanī, positioned unusually to the north of Manamaiju—despite the general pattern of Indrāyaṇī shrines in Kīrtipur, Thimi, Patan, Bhaktapur, and Nuwakot, which are oriented eastward and located at the north-western edge of settlements. Architecturally, the Manamayju Pīṭha also faces east but occupies a northern location relative to the village.The large clearing is demarcated by rest houses (phalcā) and raised platforms (sataḥ) on either side of the shrine. The entrance features a stonetoraṇadated to 1695 (NS 815), flanked by a pair of stone lions inscribed in 1672 (NS 792). Inside, a quadrangular courtyard encloses the central shrine, withphalcāstructures on both sides. Thepīṭhahouses three uncarved stones regarded as Indrāyaṇī and attendant deities; the central stone is considered the principal form of the goddess and is crowned with a carvedkīrtimukhatoraṇa. Above the stone is a smallśikhara-type pavilion sheathed in metal plates, over which stands a one-storeyedtalle-style temple roofed with metal sheets. Three gilded finials (gajūra), each holding a flutteringpatāḥ, surmount the roof.The earliest inscription on the site dates to 1672 (NS 792), referring to the installation of the lion statues and confirming thepīṭha’s existence by that time. Later inscriptions indicate the progressive addition of structures and objects. One long record documents a land grant made during the reign of King Gīrvāṇayuddha for ritual worship in the name of his mother. Although the 2015 (VS 2072) earthquake damaged portions of the temple atop thepīṭhaand the adjoiningphalcāandsataḥ, the structures did not collapse. In 2025 (VS 2081), these three components were reconstructed by Tārakeśvara Municipality; the originaljhĩgaṭīroofing was replaced with copper sheeting during this restoration.TheDevamālā Vaṃśāvalīpreserves several references to Manamayju. According to this chronicle, King Guṇakāmadeva established the Manamayju Pīṭha north of Kathmandu in 3825 of the Kalī era (N. Yogī VS 2013, p. 42). It also states that King Amara Malla settled a community of 300 households and established thepīṭha—along with initiating ritual dances—in 1483 (NS 603) (N. Yogī VS 2013, p. 96). TheSvayambhūpurāṇanarrates that at the confluence of the Keshavatī and Vimalāvatī rivers—called Manorathatīrtha—Indra united with a homely young woman named Manamaiju and, instead of taking her to heaven, elevated her to the status of Indrāyaṇī (B. Vajrācārya VS 1128, pp. 38–39).Maintenance of thepīṭhahas traditionally been overseen by the Maharjan clan, who cultivate the land endowed by King Gīrvāṇayuddha and take turns conducting the daily worship (nityapūjā) andārati. Each member assumes responsibility for one year. A second set of daily rites is performed by members of the Manamayju Devī Guṭhī, giving the shrine two distinct cycles of regular worship.The annual festival of Manamayju Ajimā, or Indrāyaṇī, is celebrated for five days from the fourteenth of dark fortnight to the third of the bright fortnight of Caitra. On the morning of the fourteenth, a ceremonial pole (yaḥsiṃ) is erected before thepīṭha, and the deity from thedyaḥchẽis carried in a palanquin (khaṭa) to the shrine in the evening. Overnight, Vajrācāryas perform esoteric rites, placing the deity’s image upon the uncarved stone of thepīṭha. The following morning, devotees gather in large numbers to offer worship, including animal sacrifice. On the first day, the palanquin is taken through the neighbourhoods of the settlement; on the second day, it remains at rest while devotional singing takes place at thedyaḥchẽ; on third, the procession is restricted to the southern precinct, after which the image is returned to thedyaḥchẽat night.During Daśaĩ, devotees may offer animal sacrifices according to personal vow. Newars of Kathmandu traditionally visit ninetīrthaover the nine days of the festival, worshipping the associated goddesses; on the sixth, this includes bathing at Manorathatīrtha—the confluence of the Keśāvatī and Vimalāvatī rivers—followed by a visit to the Manamayju Pīṭha (B. Maharjana VS 2080, p. 5). Earlier, it was customary to dedicate live animals such as goats, he-buffaloes, and sheep to the deity; however, due to the decline of grazing land and livestock keeping, this practice has nearly disappeared (local resident, Maharjan, male, age 69).
description_ne: फुसिंख्यः (मनमैजु) निवासी नेवारको ग्रामदेवता (क्षेत्रपाल)का रूपमा रहेकी इन्द्रायणीको यस पीठलाई ठमेल निवासी प्रधान खलकले भने आफ्ना इष्टदेवीका रूपमा पूज्दै आएका हुन् ।फुसिंख्यः अर्थात् मनमैजु उपत्यकाको उत्तर-पश्चिम कुनामा पर्ने नेवार बस्ती हो र यहाँ आरध्य देवीको रूपमा इन्द्रायणीलाई लिइएको छ । यहाँ स्थापित इन्द्रायणीको ‘मनमैजु’ नाम बढी प्रसिद्ध र प्रचलित छ । मनमैजुको बोलीचालीमा प्रचलित अर्को नाम ‘फुसिंख्यःअजिमा’ हो । बस्तीभित्र मनमैजुको द्यःछेँ र बाहिर पीठ रहेको छ । बस्ती बाहिर करिब १० रोपनी खुला चौरमाझ इन्द्रायणीको पीठ छ । इन्द्रायणीको पीठ प्राय पूर्वाभिमुख हुने गर्दछ र बस्तीको उत्तर-पश्चिम कोणमा स्थापित हुने गर्दछ (जस्तै कीर्तिपुर, थिमि, पाटन, भक्तपुर र नुवाकोटको इन्द्रायणी पीठ) । यहाँ पीठ पूर्वाभिमुख नै छ तर अपवादका रूपमा मनमैजु बस्तीबाट उत्तरतर्फ अवस्थित छ । खुला चौरमाझ दायाँ-बायाँ सतः एवं फल्चा बनाई पीठ अवस्थित परिसर छुट्याइएको छ । पीठमा प्रवेश गर्ने ढोकामा नेसं ८१५ (सन् १६९५) मा बनेको ढुङ्गाको तोरण छ । यस ढोकाको दायाँ-बायाँ नेसं ७९२ (सन् १६७२) का एक जोडा शिलाका सिंह प्रतिमा छन् । ढोकाभित्र चतुष्कोणाकार परिसर छ जसको केन्द्रमा पीठ छ भने दायाँ-बायाँ फल्चा बनेका छन् । पीठमा अमूर्त ढुङ्गा छ जसलाई इन्द्रायणी र अन्य देवगण मानी पूजिँदै आएको छ । अमूर्त ढुङ्गामध्ये बीचकोलाई गणकी मुख्य देवी इन्द्रायणी मानिन्छ जसमाथि शिलाको कीर्तिमुख तोरण पनि हालिएको छ । पीठमाथि शिखराकार सानो देवल बनाई धातुको पाताले मोडिएको छ । यी संरचनामाथि एक तलाको तल्ले शैलीमा मन्दिर उठाइएको छ जसको छाना धातुले छाइएको छ । छानामाथि तीनवटा सुवर्ण गजूर छन् जसमा पताः पनि झुण्ड्याइएको छ ।यस पीठमा प्राप्त सबैभन्दा पुरानो अभिलेख नेसं ७९२ (सन् १६७२) हो जसमा यहाँ सिंह प्रतिमामा स्थापनाको कुरो छ । यसबाट सो समयमै पीठको अस्तित्व रहेको ठहर्छ । पीठमा क्रमश विविध वस्तु थपिँदै गएको तथ्य यहाँ प्राप्त अभिलेख्य प्रमाणबाट थाहा हुन्छ । यहाँ राजा गीर्वाणयुद्धको समयमा उनकी आमाको नाममा पूजाका खातिर जग्गाको व्यवस्था गरिएको एक लामो अभिलेख छ । पछिल्लो महाभुकम्पमा पीठमाथि बनेको मन्दिर र दायाँ-बायाँका फल्चा-सतःका केही भागमा क्षति पुगे तापनि ढलेको भने थिएन । विसं २०८१ (सन् २०२५) मा यी तीनै संरचनालाई तारकेश्वर नगरपालिकाले पुनर्निर्माण गरेको हो । तीनै संरचनामा विगत झिंगटीको छाना हुने गरकोमा उक्त पुनर्निर्माणका दौरान तामाको पाताले मोडिएको थियो । देवमाला वंशावलीमा मनमैजुका प्रसंगहरू भेटिन्छन् । सो वंशालवली अनुसार कलिगत संवत् ३८२५ मा राजा गुणकामदेवले काठमाडौंको उत्तरमा मनमैजुको पीठ बनाएका थिए (N. Yogī VS 2013, p. 42) । यसै वंशावलीमा राजा अमर मल्लले नेसें ६०३ मा ३०० घरको बस्ती बसाली मनमैजुको पीठ स्थापना गर्नुका साथै नाच चलाएका हुन् भनिएको छ (N. Yogī VS 2013, p.96) । स्वय्‌म्भू पुराणमा यस स्थानको खोलाको दोभान (मनोरथतीर्थ) को बखान गर्दै देवराज इन्द्रले यहाँकी मनमैजु नामक एक कुरुप युवतीसँग सहवास गरेको तर उनलाई स्वर्गमा नलगी यही इन्द्रायणीको दर्जा दएको प्रसंग छ (B. Vajrācārya VS 1128, p. 38-39) ।यहाँ  गीर्वाणयुद्धले व्यवस्थआ गरेको गुठीको जग्गा जोट्दै आएका महर्जन खलकले पालैपालो नित्यपूजाको जिम्मा लिई पीठ रेखदेखको जिम्मा सम्हाल्दै आएको छ । प्रति सदस्य एक वर्षका अवधिले नित्य पूजा एवं आरतीको जिम्मेवारी हस्तान्तरण हुने गर्दछ । अर्को नित्यपूजा र आरती मनमैजु देवी गुठीका सदस्यले गर्ने गर्छन् । यसरी पीठमा दुईवटा नित्यपूजा र आरतीको प्रचलन छ । प्रतिवर्ष चैत्र महिनाकको चतुर्दशी देखि तृतीयासम्म पाँचदिन मनमैजु अजिमा अर्थात् इन्द्रायणीको जात्रा हुने गर्दछ । चतुर्दशीको विहानी पीठ अगाडि यःसिं ठड्याइन्छ भने द्यःछेँका देवीलाई खटमा राखी बेलुकी यहाँ पुर्याइन्छ ।  रातभर बज्राचार्यद्वारा देवीको मूर्तिलाई पीठको अमूर्त ढुङ्गामाथि राखी तान्त्रिक विधिबाट पूजा सम्पन्न गरिन्छ । भोलिपल्टको विहानीदेखि पीठमा बलि सहित पूजा गर्ने सर्वसाधारणको भीड लाग्ने गर्दछ । प्रतिपदाको दिनभर खटलाई बस्तीको टोल-टोलमा घुमाइन्छ । द्वितीयाको दिन खटलाई नचलाई विश्रामावस्थामा राखिन्छ तर द्यःछेँमा भने भजनकीर्तन हुने गर्दछ । तृतीयाको दिन द्यःछेँबाट दक्षिणमा पर्ने परिसरमा मात्र खटजात्रा गरी बेलुकीको प्रहरमा मूर्तिलाई द्यःछेँमै फर्काइन्छ ।पीठमा दशैंका दौरान इच्छा अनुसार बलिपूजा हुने गर्दछ । काठमाडौंवासी नेवारहरू दशैंको नौ दिन नौ तीर्थको यात्रा गरी तीर्थसम्बद्ध देवीको दर्शन गर्ने थिति छ । यस थिति अन्तर्गत षष्ठीका दिन मनोरथतीर्थ (केशावती र विमलावती नदीको संगम) मा स्नान गरी यस मनमैजु पीठमा दर्शनार्थ पुग्ने चलन छ (B. Maharjana VS 2080, p.5) ।  देवीका नाममा जिउँदा बोका, राँगा, भेडा आदि पीठमा जिउँदै छोड्ने थिति पनि थियो जुन चरण क्षेत्रको अभाव र वस्तु पालनमा आएको कमीका कारण लोपावस्थामा पुगेको छ (local resident, Maharjan, male, age 69) ।

historical_events.event_description: Rājakumāra Bhāro, Vekhāsiṃha, Manahorā, and other members jointly dedicated a pair of stone lion statues in front of the shrine. Identical inscriptions bearing this description are engraved on both statues.

The inscription is engraved on both the left and right sides of the stonetoraṇa(MAN0010–014). Although the date of the inscription can be discerned, most of the letters have eroded. Among the legible portions, the name Ramakṛṣṇa appears as one of the donors.

An activity was carried out at the shrine, though the specific nature of the work remains uncertain due to the erosion of the inscription. Among the legible portions, the name Nārāyaṇī appears as one of the contributors.

Mucā Bhāro of Thã Bahī (Thamel) constructed a capāḥ on the eastern side of the open ground of Indrāyaṇī. He also endowed land to support the annual rituals associated with the newly built capāḥ. The inscription stipulates that, after his death, apiṇḍashould be offered annually on the anniversary of his passing from the income generated by the endowed land. Additionally, it prescribes offerings to be made on the occasion of the Indrāyaṇī palanquin festival.
During the reign of King Girvāṇayuddha Śāha, lands were endowed to provide a regular income for conducting the deity’s rituals. The endowment was made in the name of the king’s mother.

A wooden embossed inscription, now in the collection of a local resident, praises the then Prime Minister Candra Śamśera. It is believed that the inscription was installed on the occasion of his visit to the Indrāyaṇī Shrine. During the later reconstruction period, the inscription was collected and preserved by a nearby resident.
The shrine premises was renovated during the reign of King Mahendra.

Under the leadership of Śiva Khatrī, a bell weighing over 28 kilograms was installed in front of the Indrāyaṇī shrine. The names of all contributors and the details of the collected funds for this undertaking are recorded in the inscription.
A bell was installed in front of the shrine. This is the same bell mentioned in the inscription dated V.S. 2042 (1986CE). The date of the offering is also inscribed on the surface of the bell.
One of thepataḥs (banners) hung on the roof bears an inscription. The inscription records only the date of the offering, commemorating the offering of the banner on that particular day.
A bell was installed in front of the shrine; however, the inscription does not record the name of the donor.
One of thepataḥs (banners) hung on the roof bears an inscription. The inscription records only the date of the offering, commemorating the offering of the banner on that particular day.
In memory of Nhuchẽ Maharjana and Caityamāyā Maharjan, all members of their family jointly offered apatāḥ(sacred banner).

The Municipality rebuilt thephalcālocated in the south of the shrine. While the overall design follows the original structure, the roof has been replaced with copper sheets instead of the traditional tiles.

Thesataḥ(MAN0010-018), which has aphalcāon its ground floor, was reconstructed by the Municipality. While the overall design follows the original structure, the roof has been replaced with copper sheets instead of the traditional tiles.
Sūrya Kumāra Cakradhara and Sānumāyā Cakradhara of Thimi offered a banner in the name of Indrāyaṇī.
